THE REPORT OF THE GENERAL SECRETARY 
OF THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION OF MONTREAL 
FOR THE YEAR ENDING MARCH 31ST, 1932. 


AS REQUIRED BY OUR CONSTITUTION AND BY-LAWS, THE 
8{ST ANNUAL REPORT INDICATING SOME OF THE ACHIEVEMENTS 
OF THE YEAR, AND OF THE CONDITION AND NEEDS OF THE ASSOCH- 
1ATION, 1S HEREBY SUBMITTED. j 


THE S!ZE AND COMPLEXITY OF OUR ORGANIZATION IN 
ITS BRANCHES AND DEPARTMENTS MAKES IT OBVIOUSLY QUITE 
IMPOSSIBLE TO DO JUSTICE IN THIS REPORT TO THE IMMENSE 
AMOUNT OF SERVICE RENDERED; ANO THE IMPORTANCE OF THE 
BRANCH ANNUAL MEETINGS AND THE PUBLICITY GIVEN IN THE COL- 
UMNS OF THE DAILY PRESS. ARE INCREASINGLY NECESSARY TO A 
FULL KNOWLEDGE OF OUR WORKe 


THE PAST YEAR HAS BEEN A MOMENTOUS ONEe THE ECON- 
OMIC DEPRESSION WHICH HAS HELD THE WHOLE WORLO IN ITS GRIP, 
HAS DEEPLY AFFECTED OUR CITY AND THE WORK OF THE YoMeCeoAs, 
AND WHILE IT HAS MADE SERIOUS FINANCIAL PROBLEMS FOR US, 
IT HAS OPENEO DOORS OF SERVICE IN A DEGREE! UNPARALLELED 
IN OUR HISTORY, WITH THE RESULT THAT THE RECORD (S AN 
UNUSUALLY GOOD ONE. IF ONE WERE TO SUMMARIZE THE OUTSTAND- 
ING FEATURES, 1!T WOULD PERHAPS BE FAIR TO CITE; FIRST, 
THE OPENING OF THE NEW STANLEY STREET BUILDING AND THE 
EXTRAORDINARY INCREASE IN SERVICE AT THAT POINT; SECOND, 
THE PLACING AT THE SERVICE OF YOUNG MEN AND BOYS OUT OF 
WORK ALL THE RESOURCES OF THE ASSOCIATION; THIRD, THE 
SHARING IN THE WORLO ASSEMBLIES FOR BOYS ANDO YOUNG MEN 
AT TORONTO IN JULY, AND THE WORLO'S CONFERENCE ANO INTER= 
NATIONAL CONVENTION IN CLEVELAND IN AUGUST; AND FOURTH, 
THE UNCEASING EFFORT OF THE CONTROLLING GROUP TO DO A 
MUCH LARGER WORK WITH REOUCED REVENUES. 


FOREIGN SERVICE: 


THE PRESENT DAY INTERNATIONAL SITUATION IS WITH- 
OUT PARALLEL IN HISTORY. THE COMBINATION OF FORCES WHICH, 
SINCE THE CLOSE OF THE GREAT WAR, HAVE BEEN AT WORK UNDER- 
MINING THE WORLD'S ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL SYSTEM REACHED 
A CLIMAX IN 4931, WITH A SUBSEQUENT WORLOWICE UPHEAVAL 
AND DISTRESS. ONE HAS ONLY TO THINK OF WAR REPARATIONS 
AND DEBTS, THE ACCUMULATION OF THE MAJOR PORTION OF THE 
WORLD'S SUPPLY OF FREE GOLD AT TWO CENTRES, THE EFFORT 
TO RAISE TARIFF WALLS IN ALMOST EVERY COUNTRY, THE GRAVE 
AND OMINOUS DEVELOPMENTS IN MANCHURIA ANO SHANGHAI, TO 
REALIZE HOW SERIOUS ARE OUR WORLD PROBLEMS. WE MUST CON- 
STANTLY REMIND OURSELVES THAT ANY SOLUTION OF THESE GREAT 
QUESTIONS CAN ONLY REST ON A MORAL FOUNDATION AND NOT ON 
ONE OF FORCE. IF THIS FAILS, OUR PLIGHT WILL INDEED BE 
A SERIOUS ONE. 


SO FAR FROM BEING DISCOURAGED, THE YeMeCeAs MUST 
FIND IN THESE HAPPENINGS A NEW CHALLENGE AND A NEW STIM- 
ULUS TO CARRY ON ITS WORLD SERVICE PROGRAM, LCOKING TO 


te 


THE TIME WHEN MUTUAL UNDERSTANDING, GOODWILL AND CO-OPER- 
ATION MAY PREVAIL IN INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS« MANY THINGS 
ARE HAPPENING THESE DAYS WHICH GIVE US COURAGE. MEN OF 
AFFAIRS, ORAWN FROM MANY LANDS, (IN MANY CONFERENCES, HAVE 
DEALT FRANKLY AND WISELY WITH INTERNATIONAL PROBLEMS AND 
HAVE CLEARLY STATED THE ESSENTIAL FACTS REGARDING THEM, 
INCREASINGLY, TOO, PUBLIC OPINION IS HELPING TO INFLUENCE 
THE WORLD SITUATION AND TO CREATE THAT ATMOSPHERE OF CON- 
FIDENCE AND MUTUAL TRUST IN WHICH GOODWILL THRIVES> 


THE MONTREAL ASSOCIATION HAS CONTINUED TO PLAY A 
WORTHY PART IN THIS FIELD. OUR CITY WAS ONE OF FOUR OR 
FIVE PORTS OF ENTRY USED BY MANY DELEGATES TO THE WORLO'S 
Boys AND YOUNG MEN'S ASSEMBLIES AT TORONTO IN JULY, AND 
THE WORLD'S CONFERENCE AT CLEVELAND IN AUGUSTe AOORESSES 
BY DRe TeZe KOO OF CHINA, AND DRe JOHN Re MOTT, §N ADVANCE 
OF THESE MEETINGS, WERE OF GREAT IMPORTANCE IN INTERPRET] 
ING THEIR WORLD CHARACTER AND SIGNIFICANCEs THEN, TOO, 
THE CONTACTS WITH OVERSEAS DELEGATES PASSING THROUGH OUR 
CITY, AND THE ATTENDANCE OF THPRTY-FIVE REPRESENTATIVES 
FROM MONTREAL AND THEIR ADDRESSES UPON THEIR RETURN, MADE 
AN IMPORTANT CONTRIGUTION TO THE EDUCATION OF OUR CONSTIT=- 
UENCY ON INTERNATOONAL AFFAIRS. 


MR. Ge ERNEST TRUEMAN DELIVERED SIXTY ADDRESSES 
DURING THE YEAR AND HAS MADE AN IMPORTANT CONTRIBUTION 
TQ OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE CRITICAL SITUATION IN THE 
FAR EAST. MRe ROBERT O. BUELL, FELLOWSHIP SECRETARY 
FROM INDIA, ALSO MADE NUMEROUS AODRESSES ON INDIA PRIOR 
TO HIS LEAVING IN SEPTEMBER. MRe TeDe SANTWAN, HIS 
SUCCESSOR, EXECUTIVE SECRETARY OF ONE OF THE BRANCHES 
OF THE CALCUTTA ASSOCIATION, MADE A FURTHER CONTRIBUTION 
TO OUR UNDERSTANOING OF INDIA. THESE SECRETARIES HAVE 
LEFT A DEEP IMPRESSION UPON OUR MEMBERS AND FRIENDS, AND 
HAVE WITHOUT DOUBT MADE FOR A NEW UNDERSTANDING OF SOME 
OF OUR PROBLEMS OF EMPIRE. 


FOLLOWING THE WORLO'S CONFERENCE, MRe WeBe CAPEK, 
FROM PRAGUE, CZECHO-SLOVAKIA, SPENT THREE WEEKS AS OUR 
GUEST, OBSERVING THE WORK OF OUR BRANCHES, AND GIVING 
US THE OPPORTUNITY TO LEARN OF THE SITUATION IN TRAT 
COUNTRY

NATIONAL WORK: 


THE NATIONAL COUNCIL OF THE YeMeCeA*S OF CANADA 
HELD THEIR ANNUAL MEETING IN MONTREAL FOR THE FIRST TIME 
IN TEN YEARS, WHICH WAS ATTENDED BY REPRESENTATIVES FROM 
ALL THE PROVINCES WITH THE EXCEPTION OF ALBERTA. THIS 
MEETING WAS HELD IN°OUR CITY WITH A VIEW TO GIVING THE 
DELEGATES AN OPPORTUNITY TO SEE THE WORK IN OUR SOUTH- 
WESTERN BRANCH AND THE NEW ADDITION AND REMODELLED FAC- 
ILITIES IN OUR’ DRUMMONO-STANLEY STREET BUILDING. ONE 
COULD NOT BUT FEEL THAT DRe EeMe. BEST OF OUR OWN CITY, 
WHO LAST JULY ASSUMED THE DUTIES OF GENERAL SECRETARY OF 
THE NATIONAL COUNCIL, HAD TAKEN ON HIS WORK IN A VERY 
OIFFICULT PERIOD AND YET IT WAS A CAUSE FOR GRATITUDE 
THAT IN THESE TRYING TIMES OUR MOVEMENT HAD ONE OF HIS 
GENIUS AS ITS EXECUTIVE HEAD. TWO ASSOCIATIONS, EeGe, 
SYONEY AND GLACE BAY, NeoSe, WERE FORCED TO SUSPEND OPER- 
ATIONS OURING THE YEAR, WHEREAS LETHBRIDGE, WHICH HAD 
NOT OPERATED IN OUR MOVEMENT FOR SEVEN OR EIGHT YEARS, 
WAS RE“ORGANIZEO. THE ANNUAL MEETING OF THE COUNCIL, 
HAS COME TO BE ONE OF THE MAJOR EVENTS IN THE LIFE OF 
CANADIAN ASSOCIATIONS, AND THE DISCUSSIONS AND (INSPIRAT- 
'ONAL ADDRESSES ARE ON A HIGH LEVEL AND MEAN MUCH TO 
OUR MOVEMENT THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY. ONE OF THE oUT- 
STANDING FUNCTIONS IN CONNECTION WITH THIS MEETING WAS 
THE RECEPTION GIVEN IN THEIR OWN HOME BY MR. AND MRS. 
GERALD We BIRKS. 


SUMMARY _OF EXPANSION CAMPAIGN: 


IT WAS FIVE YEARS AGO LAS NOVEMBER THAT THE FIRST 


DEFINITE STEP: WAS TAKEN IN CONNECTION WITH OUR EXPANSION 
CAMPAIGN. ON-THE OCCASION OF OUR 75TH ANNIVERSARY DINNER 


IN 1926, THE NEED FOR THE CAMPAIGN, AS OISCLOSEO BY OUR 
SURVEY, AND AN INITIAL GIET OF $100,00.00 WAS ANNOUNCED. 
iN 1928 A FINANCIAL CAMPAIGN FOR $1,500,000.00 WAS HELD, 
WHEN $4)300;00.00 WAS. SECURED, OF WHICH $50,000.00 WAS 
CONDITIONAL ON THE FULL. AMOUNT BEING RAISED. IN 1929 THE 
BALANCE OF THE MONEY WAS SUBSCRIBED, ANDO THE CONSTRUCTION 
OF THE SOUTHWESTERN BRANCH WAS COMMENCED. IN 1930, THE 
BUILDING WAS COMPLETED, AND FORMALLY OPENED IN FEBRUARY, 
PROPERTY IN NOTRE DAME DE GRACE WAS BOUGHT AND DEVELOPED 
IN THE SAME PERIOD, AND THE ORGANIZATION OF A BRANCH IN 
THAT DISTRICT EFFECTED. IN 1930, ALSO, A CONTRACT WAS 
LET FOR THE STANLEY STREET ADDITION TO: THE DRUMMOND STREET 
BUILOINGe THIS WORK WAS COMPLETED, AND THE BUILDING 
OPENED IN APRIL 19316 : 


DURING THE PAST YEAR, THE CONSOLICATION OF OUR 
SOUTHWESTERN BRANCH, THE SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS COLLEGE, 
THE CENTRAL BRANCH AND THE RESIDENCE BUILDING, AND THE 
FINAL DEVELOPMENT OF THE COMMUNITY PROGRAM IN NOTRE 
DAME DE GRACE WAS EFFECTED. THERE NOW REMAINS THE TASK 
OF SECURING PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDING PLEDGES TO ENABLE US 
TO PROCEED WITH FULFILLMENT OF OUR PROMISES TO NOTRE 
DAME DE GRACEe 


THIS FIVE*YEAR PERIOB® HAS BEEN A MOST ADVENTUR= 
OUR ONE, AND HAS BROUGHT THE ASSOCIATION'S SERVICE TO 
A LEVEL OF EFFECTIVENESS THAT IS VERY ENCOURAGING. ' 
EVERY EFFORT SHOULD BE MADE, HOWEVER, TO COMPLETE THE 
TASK WHICH WE SET OUT TO ACCOMPLISH, NOTWITHSTANDING © 
THE ADVERSE CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH WE LABOUR. WE SHOULD 
REMIND OURSELVES THAT, WITH EVERY FIVE YEARS, A GENERATION 
OF BOYS, IN THE MOST FORMATIVE PERIOD OF THEIR LIVES, | 
PASS BY AND ARE FOREVER GONE BEYONO THE INFLUENCE OF THE 
ASSOCIATION TO AFFECT THEIR LIVES FOR GOOD.

METROPOLITAN RESIDENCE BUILDING: 

THE YEAR JUST CLOSED HAS PROVEN THE VALUE OF 
OUR NEW PLAN OF ADMINISTRATION WHEREBY THE DRUMMOND= 
STANLEY STREET BUILDING 1S OPERATED BY A SPECIAL COMM- 
ITTEE OF THE METROPOLITAN BOARD. THE STRIKING ADVANCE 
IN PROGRAM IN THE CENTRAL BRANCH, WHICH HAS BEEN ONE OF 
THE OUTSTANDING ACCOMPLISHMENTS OF THE YEAR, HAS BEEN 


0 Ee 


FACILITATED BY THE NEW ARRANGEMENT WHICH HAS ENABLED 
THE STAFF, BOARD AND COMMITTEES OF BOTH THE CENTRAL 
BRANCH AND THE COLLEGE, TO CONCENTRATE ON PROGRAM 
WITHOUT DIRECT RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE DETAILED ADMIN] 
ISTRATION OF THE BUILDING. 


IT tS OF SPECIAL INTEREST THAT OF THE 601 
ROOMS §N THE OLD AND NEW BUILDINGS, 422 WERE OCCUPIED 
ON FEBRUARY 6TH, THE LOWEST NUMBER BEING ON DECEMBER 
24TH WHEN 272 MEN WERE IN RESIDENCE. SINCE THE OPENING 
OF OUR NEW FISCAL YEAR, THE NUMBER HAS BEEN INCREASED 
TO 476 ON MAY 3RD, OR 80% OF THE TOTAL NUMBER OF ROOMS 
AVAILABLE. IN ALL, 5,376 DIFFERENT MEN WERE IN RESI- 
DENCE. TWO HUNDRED AND SEVENTY=FIVE MEN WHO WERE OUT 
OF WORK OR IN SPECIAL NEEO OF ASSISTANCE WERE GIVEN 
ACCOMMODATION AT VERY SPECIAL RATES IN NO CASE EXCEED- 
ING SEVENTY“FIVE PER CENT OF THE MINIMUM RATES, 


SECRETARIAL STAFF: 


DURING RHE PAST YEAR WE HAVE HAD THIRTY-EIGHT 
SECRETARIES ON OUR REGULAR STAFF AS COMPARED WITH 
THIRTY*THREE DURING THE TWO PRECEDING YEARS. THIS 
NUMBER WAS REDUCED BY THREE BY MARCH 31ST, ONE BY 
RESIGNATION, ONE BY TRANSFER, ANO ONE BY RETIREMENTs 
SUBSEQUENT TO THAT TIME, TWO OTHER SECRETARIES HAVE 
RETIRED, MAKING A REDUCTION OF FIVE IN ALL, NONE OF 
WHOM HAVE BEEN REPLACED. THE FACT THAT WE ARE NOW 
CARRYING ON WITH NO INCREASE IN THE STAFF OVER THE 
YEAR 1929 IS THE MORE REMARKABLE WHEN ONE CONS! DERS 
THAT THE ASSOCIATION IN THE LAST YEAR HAS ADDED ITS 
LARGE STANLEY STREET BUILDING TO ITS EXISTING EQUIP} 
MENT AND HAS OPENED WHAT {S TANTAMOUNT TO A NEW BRANCH, 
FOR THE WHITE=COLLAR GROUP, WITH HEADQUARTERS IN THE 
SUN LIFE BUILDING, TO WHICH ONE SECRETARY, FOR THE 
PAST SEVEN MONTHS, HAS DEVOTED HIS ENTIRE TIME. THE 
TOTAL STAFF OF THE ASSOCIATION ON MARCH 31ST NUMBER- 
EO 163 EMPLOYEES AND 50 TEACHERS. THE LATTER GROUP 
WERE ALL ON PART TIME, AS WERE FOUR SECRETARIES.

MEMBERSHIP: 


THE PAID MEMBERSHIP OF THE ASSOCIATION ON MARCH 
31ST WAS 6,492 AS COMPARED WITH 6,479 AS YEAR AGO, AN 
INCREASE OF 13. THERE WERE, HOWEVER, FREE MEMBERSHIPS 
ISSUED TO 1,284 UNEMPLOYED BOYS AND YOUNG MEN, AND 1F 
THIS LATTER GROUP BE COUNTED AS MEMBERS THERE 1S AN 
INCREASE ON THE YEAR OF 1,297. A SERIES OF MEMBERSHIP 
CAMPAIGNS WAS CARRIED ON BY OUR BRANCHES LAST OCTOBER, 
OURING THE COURSE OF WHICH NEARLY SIX HUNDRED MEMBERS 
WERE SECURED IN THE COMBINEO EFFORT. THIS EFFORT PRO- 
BABLY SAVED THE ASSOCIATION FROM.HAVING A DECREASE IN 
THE ENROLMENT OF ITS PAID UP MEMBERSHIP. THE FIGURES 
GIVEN, OF COURSE, DO NOT INCLUDE THE HUNDREOS OF YOUNG 
MEN AND BOYS WHO BECAME MEMBERS OF THE ASSOCIATION 
ONLY FOR’ THE SUMMER MONTHS OR TO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OUR 
SHORT TERM MEMBERSHIP, NOR DO THEY INCLUDE THE THOUS- 
ANDS OF YOUNG PEOPLE WHO USE OUR DIFFERENT BUILOINGS 
AS COMMUNITY CENTRES, NOR THE CONSTANT STREAM OF NEW- 
COMERS TO OUR CITY AND OTHERS WHO ARE SERVED BY THE 
ASSOCIATION WITHOUT REGARD TO THE FACT OF THEIR MEMB-

UNEMPLOYMENT: 


ALMOST FROM ITS INCEPTION, THE YeMeCeA. IN 
MONTREAL HAS TAKEN A DEEP AND HELPFUL INTEREST IN “SECUR- 
ING EMPLOYMENT FOR YOUNG MENe HUNDREDS OF MEN IN THIS 
CITY BEAR TESTIMONY TO THE FACT THAT THE ASSOCIATION 
SECURED FOR THEM A POSITION UPON COMING TO MONTREAL. 

THE INTEREST OF THE "¥" HAS ALWAYS BEEN VERY MUCH DEEP- 
ER THAN THAT OF HELPING TO SECURE A POSITION, AND INC- 
LUDES ADVICE AND COUNSEL ON MANY SUBYECTS, AND THE 
OPPORTUNITY FOR ENRICHMENT OF LIFE BY PARTICIPATION IN 
THE PROGRAM OF THE "Y¥", 


AS THE PRESENT ECONOMIC DEPRESSION WIDENED, 
THE ASSOCIATION'S SERVICE TO THE UNEMPLOYED GROUP DEEP}- 
ENED. A GREAT STIMULUS WAS GIVEN TO THIS MINISTRY BY 


A SERIES OF INFORMAL CONFERENCES OF CANADJAN DELEGATES 

iNG INTERVALS OF THE INTERNATIONAL CONVENTION LAST 
SUMMER AT CLEVELAND, IT WAS AGREEC THAT THE CANADIAN 
ASSOCIATIONS SHOULD MAKE A FORMAL OFFER OF ITS SERVICES 
TO THE PRIME MINISRER WITH THE CONVICTION THAT EVEN IF 
IT WERE POSSIBLE, BY A GREAT OUTPOURING OF UNSELFISH- 
NESS, TO SEE THAT NO MAN, WOMAN OR CHILD SHOULD SUFFER 
FROM LACK OF FOOD, SHELTER OR CLOTHING, THERE WAS AN 
EQUAL DUTY UPON US ALL TO FULLY PROTECT THE PHYSICAL, 
SOCIAL, MORAL AND SPIRITUAL HEALTH OF THE NATION ON 
THE THEORY THAT “MAN CANNOT LIVE BY BREAD ALONE". OUR 
PRESIDENT, WITH THE GENERAL SECRETARY AND THE CHAIRMAN 
oF THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE OF THE NATIONAL COUNCIL, 
SUBSEQUENTLY PROCEEDED TO OTTAWA IN SEPTEMBER ANDO 
FORMALLY OFFERED THE RESOURCES OF THE Y.M.C.A°S IN 
CANADA IN HELPING SOLVE THE PROBLEMS ARISING OUT OF 
THE UNEMPLOYMENT SITUATION. THIS OFFER WAS ACCEPTED 
BY THE PREMIER AND COMMUNICATED BY HIM TO THE PROVINC- 
{AL PREMIERS. 


CONCURRENTLY WITH THESE DISCUSSIONS, THE 
MONTREAL COUNCIL OF SOCIAL AGENCIES FORMALLY REQUESTED 
THE MONTREAL ASSOCIATION TO CO-GPERATE WITH THEM IN 
PROVIDING EMPLOYMENT SERVICE AND, IF NECESSARY, RELIEF 
FOR THE OFFICE, CLERICAL AND PROFESSIONAL GROUPS OF 
UNEMPLOYED, WHICH WORK THE SUN LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY 
HAD CARRIEO ON AT THEIR OWN EXPENSE FOR OVER ONE YEAR 
AND WERE NOW OBLIGED TO DISCONTINUE. THE ASSOCIATION 
PROMPTLY APPOINTED MRe Wede HOLLIDAY TO TAKE CHARGE OF 
THIS WORK ANO ACCEPTED THE OFFER OF THE SUN LIFE ASSUR- 
ANCE COMPANY TO PROVIDE THE NECESSARY SPACE AND EQUIP- 
MENT IN THEIR HEAO OFFICE BUILDING AS HEADQUARTERS. 

AS A RESULT, 1,660 MEN HAVE BEEN REGISTERED UP To THE 
PRESENTe THE AMOUNT OF MONEY DISBURSED TO DATE IN 
OIRECT RELIEF HAS TOTALLED $4,500.00. 


UPON THE FORMATION OF THE MONTREAL BOYS? WORK 
COUNCIL LAST AUTUMN, THE ASSOCIATION WHOLEHEARTEOLY 
PARTICIPATED IN THE TASK OF REGISTERING AND SERVING 
SOME FIFTEEN OR SIKTEEN HUNGRED UNEMPLOYED BOYS. IN 
THE MATTER OF ENLISTING AND TRAINING MEN OF THE RIGHT 
CALIBRE TO INTERVIEW THESE LADS, THE ASSOCIATION MADE 
A NOTABLE CONTRIBUTION. OF SOME TWENTY-FOUR DISTRICTS

TO NEARLY 800 OF THESE BoYs, 


THE SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS COLLEGE OF THE ASSOC+ 
IATION GAVE BURSARIES TO OVER TWO HUNDREO STUDENTS

IN ITS RESIDENCE BUILDING ON STANLEY STREET,

THE TERRIFIC HAZARD OF PH¥SICAL, MORAL AND

RELIGIOUS WORK 


THE ASSOCIATION HAS CONTINED ITS POLICY OF 
EARNESTLY ENDEAVORING TO PLACE A CHRISTIAN EMPHASIS 
ON ALL OF ITS PROGRAM AND HAS HAD A FRUITFUL YEAR IN 
ITS SPECIFICALLY RELIGIOUS WORK. THE METHOOS USED 
INCLUDED PERSONAL INTERVIEWS, DISCUSSION AND STUDY 
GROUPS; CONFERENCE AND FORUMS; FIRESIDE SING-SONGS; 
SUNDAY AFTERNOON MUSICALES AND TEAS FOR YOUNG MEN 
LIVING AWAY FROM HOME; CAMPFIRE TALKS ANO DEVOTIONS; 
RESIDENT MEMBERS* SUNDAY MORNING BREAKFASTS; FOREIGN 
SERVICE MEETINGS; THE FELLOWSHIP BIBLE CLASS CONDUCTED 
(N THE CENTRAL BRANCH WHICH ENROLLED UP TO SEVENTY= 
FIVE MENe

OF TO-DAY, RECEIVED DIRECT COMMENDATION AT THE INTER- 
‘NATIONAL CONVENTION HELD IN CLEVELAND, WHEN THE FOLLOW- 
{NG RESOGLUTION WAS PASSED: 


mRESOLVED: 


THAT THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATIONS OF 
NORTH AMERICA SHOULD REGARD AS ONE OF THEIR FUNDAMENTAL 
PRIVILEGES AND FUNCTIONS, THE MAINTENANCE OF AN OPEN 
PLATFORM ON WHICH MAY BE DISCUSSED ALL QUESTIONS AFFECT- 
ING THE ECONOMIC, POLITICAL AND SPIRITUAL WELFARE OF THE 
COMMUNITY AND OF THE WORLD; THAT THE ASSOCIATION SHOULD 
DEVELOP AND ACTIVELY PROMOTE A PROGRAM OF SOCIAL ANO 
CHRISTIAN EDUCATION, WITH A VIEW TO HELPING TO EDUCATE 
PUBLIC OPINION FOR THE PURPOSE OF RECONSTRUCTING OUR 
SOCIAL ORDER IN THE LIGHT OF, AND UPON THE BASIS OF, THE

THE GRAMMAR SCHOOL MEETS A GREAT NEED IN THE 
CITY WHICH ARISES FROM THE LACK OF A COMPULSORY SCHOOL

AND GIRLS LEAVING SCHOOL BEFORE COMPLETING THEIR ELEMENT= 
ARY EDUCATION. CAREFULLY GRADED COURSES ARE OFFERED,

AN INTERESTING FEATURE OF THE SCHOOL !S THE SPECIAL WORK 
FOR ADULTS, SOME OF WHOM CAN NEITHER READ NOR WRITE WHEN

THE GENERAL PROGRAM OF ACTIVITIES INCLUDES GYMNe= 
ASiUM CLASSES FOR BOYS AND MEN FROM TEN YEARS TO SEVENTY 
YEARS OF AGE; AND BUILT AROUND THE CLASSES ARE ALL FORMS 
OF INDOOR GAMES AND SPORTS. 


COMPETITIVE GAMES AND SPORTS INTERESTED A LARGE 
NUMBER OF MEN AND BOYS AS WELL AS MANY WOMEN AND GIRL 
MEMBERS. REPRESENTATIVE TEAMS FROM THE BRANCHES TOOK 
PART IN OPEN CITY LEAGUES AND TOURNAMENTS AND IN INTER- 
YoMeCoAe COMPETITIONS IN BASKETBALL, SOFT BALL, HOCKEY, 
VOLLEYBALL, BADMINTON, WRESTLING, BOXING, FENCING, CROSS- 
COUNTRY RACING, GYMNASTICS, SWIMMING AND TENNIS; WHICH 
SHOWS THE WIDE RANGE OF INTEREST OF OUR MEMBERS. 


TEACHING SWIMMING TO BEGINNERS WAS FEATURED 
THROUGHOUT THE YEAR IN THE FIVE BRANCHES WHICH HAVE SWIMe- 
MING POOLS, AND SPECIAL CLASSES WERE CONDUCTED IN THE 
SUMMER FOR SMALL BOYS AND GIRLS WHO ARE NOT MEMBERS. OVER 
1,700 CHILDREN WERE GIVEN INSTRUCTION DURING THE YEAR, 


TWO INTER-BRANCH SWIMMING MEETS FOR BOYS AND AN 
INTER@BRANCH SWIMMING LEAGUE FOR MEN GAVE OPPORTUNITIES 
FOR COMPETITION TO THE GOOD SWIMMERS. 


FOUR BRANCHES WITH 23 TENNIS COURTS HAD 373 
MEMBERS; NORTH BRANCH INSTALLED LIGHTS ON FOUR COURTS 
THIS YEARe AN INTER@BRANCH LEAGUE IN MEN'S SINGLES AND 
DOUBLES, WOMEN'S SINGLES AND DOUBLES, AND MIXED DOUBLES 
WAS SUCCESSFULLY CONDUCTED ALL SUMMER, AND WAS WON BY 
NORTH BRANCH. NORTH BRANCH ALSO ENTERED A TEAM IN THE 
OUTREMONT TOURNAMENT. 


MEN'S AND BOYS’ INTER=*BRANCH LEAGUES IN SOFTBALL 
WERE CONDUCTED LAST SUMMER WITH NEARLY ALL BRANCHES PARTI- 
CIPATINGe NOTRE DAME DE GRACE BRANCH CONDUCTED AN OPEN 
LEAGUE FOR NOTRE DAME DE GRACE TEAMS AND SEVERAL BRANCHES 
PLAYED IN LOCAL CITY LEAGUES. 


BASKETBALL HELD THE USUAL LARGE PLACE IN THE

NORTH BRANCH: 


IN MAKING A DIGEST OF :'THE VARIOUS DETAILED REPORTS 
OF NORTH BRANCH, SEVERAL {TEMS STAND OUT IN BOLD RELIEF. 
THE FIRST TO BE NOTED 1S THE MANNER IN WHICH LAYMEN, 
YOUNG AND OLD, HAVE RALLIED ABOUT THE ASSOCIATION IN A 
TIME OF DIFFICULTY AND HAVE GIVEN UNSTINTINGLY OF THEIR 
TIME AND TALENTS IN ORDER THAT IN A PERIOD OF DECREASING 
SPENDING POWER THE SERVICES OF THE YeMeCeAe SHOULD NOT BE 
CURTAILED BUT RATHER EXPANDED. IT 1S WITH GREAT SATIS- 
FACTION AND PRIDE THAT -OUR BOARD OF MANAGEMENT RECOGNIZES 
THE YEOMAN SERVICE OF SUCH LOYAL AND PURPOSEFUL MEMBERS. 
WE MIGHT ALSO RECORD THE EXPANDING OF AN OLD POLICY OF 
THE ASSOCIATION, THE EXTENDING TO THOSE WHO ARE UNABLE To 
PAY FOR, BUT YET PROFIT BY AND APPRECIATE, OUR SERVICES. 
OVER TWO HUNDRED SUCH MEMBERSHIPS HAVE BEEN ISSUED THIS 
YEAR TO DESERVING YOUNG MEN AND BOYS WHO THROUGH UNEMPLOY- 
MENT HAVE BEEN UNABLE TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE FINANCIAL UP- 
KEEP OF THE INSTITUTION.’ A THIRD POINT TO REMARK IS THE 
SURPRISING MULTIPLICATION OF ACTIVITIES DURING THE-PAST 
YEAR AND THE MULTIPLICATION OF THOSE PARTICIPATING IN 
THEM, TRULY SUCH TIMES AS THESE HAVE PROVED THE GREAT 
VALUE OF OUR ASSOCIATION IN THE SERVICE OF YOUNG MEN AND 
~ BOYS OF LIMITED MEANS. WE ARE HAPPY THAT WE HAVE BEEN 
ABLE TO SERVE OUR COMMUNITY IN SUCH A TIME. TO THOSE 
WHO, IN THE SPIRIT OF THE MASTER, SEEK TO SERVE, THIS 
TIME HAS PROVEN AN ABUNDANT OPPORTUNITY. 


THE PROGRAM PROMOTED FOR BOYS AND MEN DURING THE 
YEAR INCLUDED SUPPERS WITH SPECIAL SPEAKERS, DISCUSSION 
GROUPS ON SUCH TOPICS AS CURRENT EVENTS, SEX EDUCATION, 
ASSOCIATION HISTORY AND PRINCIPLES, AND PSYCHOLOGY, 
SPECIAL INTEREST GROUPS WERE FORMED ALONG THE LINES OF 
DRAMATICS, PUBLIC SPEAKING, SHOWGARD WRITING, BASKETRY, 
FLOWER MAKING ANDO GLEE SINGING, SEVERAL DANCES WERE 
HELD, AND SEVERAL MEETINGS AFTER GYM AT WHICH TOAST AND 
TEA WERE SERVED, PROMOTING A GENERAL SPIRIT OF INTIMACY 
AND SOCIABILITY. HIKES AND PICNICS AS USUAL FEATURED 
THE SUMMER PROGRAM. 


NINETEEN HOURS OF REGULAR GYM CLASSES, BOXING 
WRESTLING, FENCING AND SWIMMING CLUBS; BASKETBALL AND 
BASEBALL LEAGUES; A TENNIS AND TWO BAOMINTON CLUBS, 
FURNISHED A WIDE RANGE OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES. THE 
ANNUALH#LEARN TO SWiM' CAMPAIGN FOR SCHOOLBOYS ENROLLED 
250 {NDI VIDUALS.

. AS FOLLOWERS OF JESUS, IT IS OUR RIGHT AND 
DUTY TO LIVE WITHOUT FEAR. WE SHOULD AS INDIVIDUALS
